title: An improved upper bound on the Ruzsa number
summary: Let $R_m$ be the least positive integer $r$ such that there exists a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_{m}$ with $A+A=\mathbb{Z}_m$ for which the number of ordered solutions of $n=x+y$ with $x,y\in A$ is at most $r$ for every $n\in \mathbb{Z}_m$. In this note we prove that $R_m\leqslant 128$ for every positive integer $m$, improving the previous bound $R_m\leqslant 192$.
